metadata.title: Security Report Guidance Patterns
metadata.description: Patterns for how security findings should be reported deterministically.

concepts.title: Terrorism
concepts.description: Promotion, support, glorification, or operational discussion of terrorism.

concepts.title: Violence
concepts.description: Physical harm, violent action, or violent escalation.

concepts.title: Public Order
concepts.description: Order, stability, compliance, and societal calm.

entries.title: Report Assembly
entries.description: Guidance for converting security analysis into a concise reviewer report.
supporting_evidence: The report should anchor the exact phrase and the specific article.
Reasoning should explain the security meaning in narrative terms.
contradictory_evidence: The report invents facts outside the chunk.
The report ignores a clear exception.
false_positives: Overstating a weak or neutral mention.
Using a broad article when a specific one fits better.
counter_examples: A report that quotes the phrase and explains the context.
A report that marks a neutral mention as review-only.
cross_sentence_indicators: A security phrase appears in one sentence and the report justification references later context.
Different articles may be combined when the same evidence supports them.
reviewer_guidance: Use the shortest exact phrase and the most specific atom.
Keep a clear distinction between finding and review-only notes.

confidence_modifiers.title: Broad Only
confidence_modifiers.description: Only a broad article is applicable.

glossary_relationships.note: Report guidance must preserve the security rationale.

gcam_mappings.note: Use as an umbrella mapping when security content affects public interest.
